slides.title: Kawasaki Disease: Must-Knows
slides.subtitle: Diagnosis, IVIG dosing & top NEET-PG traps

slides.title: CRASH
slides.subtitle: Plus Fever ≥ 5 days + ≥ 4 of 5 criteria
points: C - Conjunctivitis: Bilateral, non-purulent, spares limbus
R - Rash: Polymorphous, maculopapular (non-vesicular)
A - Adenopathy: Cervical, unilateral, node ≥ 1.5 cm
S - Strawberry tongue, cracked red lips & oral erythema
H - Hands & feet: Acute edema/erythema; late peeling
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Perineal erythema/peeling appears early in week 1!

slides.title: Incomplete (Atypical) KD
slides.subtitle: Suspect when < 4 CRASH criteria exist
points: Fever ≥ 5 days + 2–3 criteria (or infant ≤ 6 mo: fever ≥ 7 days)
Elevated inflammatory markers: CRP ≥ 3.0 mg/dL or ESR ≥ 40 mm/hr
Need ≥ 3 lab criteria or a positive echocardiogram to confirm
Labs: anemia, albumin ≤ 3 g/dL, high ALT, WBC ≥ 15k, sterile pyuria
Platelets ≥ 4.5 lakh/mm³ after day 7 of illness
slides.highlight: PYQ clue: Sterile pyuria is ≥ 10 WBC/hpf on urine microscopy!

slides.title: IVIG & Aspirin Regimen
slides.subtitle: Start promptly to protect coronaries
points: IVIG 2 g/kg single IV infusion over 10–12 hours
Best given within 10 days of fever onset (give later if active inflammation)
Aspirin 30–50 mg/kg/day PO in 4 doses (per IAP; 80–100 per US) till afebrile 48–72h
Then low-dose Aspirin 3–5 mg/kg/day PO OD for 6–8 weeks
Continue low-dose aspirin indefinitely if coronary aneurysms persist
slides.highlight: IVIG cuts coronary aneurysm risk from ~25% down to < 4%!

slides.title: IVIG-Resistant Kawasaki
slides.subtitle: Fever ≥ 36h after 1st IVIG ends (~10–20%)
points: Repeat IVIG 2 g/kg single IV infusion over 10–12 hours
OR IV Methylprednisolone 30 mg/kg/day (max 1 g) for 1–3 days
OR Infliximab 5 mg/kg single IV infusion (anti-TNF-α)
Also consider early steroids in high-risk scores (e.g. Kobayashi)
slides.highlight: Red flag: Persistent fever strongly predicts coronary aneurysms!

slides.title: Acute vs Subacute Phase
slides.subtitle: Acute (Wk 1–2) || Subacute (Wk 2–4)
points: High fever, irritability & CRASH || Fever resolves; acute signs fade
Erythema & edema of hands/feet || Periungual desquamation begins
Normal/mildly raised platelets || Thrombocytosis (often > 10 lakh/mm³)
Myocarditis & pericardial effusion || Coronary aneurysms peak
slides.highlight: Echo schedule: At diagnosis, 1–2 weeks, and 4–6 weeks!

slides.title: High-Yield Exam Traps
slides.subtitle: Last-minute NEET-PG / INI-CET pearls
points: Defer live vaccines (MMR, Varicella) for 11 months post-IVIG
Give inactivated flu vaccine on aspirin (Reye syndrome risk)
MC cause of death: Myocardial infarction from coronary thrombosis
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: MC coronary artery involved is LAD > RCA > LMCA!
